summary: Kenora Airport (YQK) serves the city of Kenora in northwestern Ontario, acting as a primary gateway to the Lake of the Woods region, one of Canada's premier freshwater fishing and wilderness recreation destinations. The airport handles scheduled regional service as well as charter and private flights, particularly during the warm-weather tourist season. Its location makes it a convenient entry point for visitors heading to lakeside cottages, fishing camps, and outdoor resorts across the region.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from Kenora Airport?
A: Regional carriers including Air Canada Express (operated by Calm Air) and Wasaya Airways provide scheduled passenger service, primarily connecting Kenora with Winnipeg and other northern Ontario communities. Seasonal and charter flights are common during the summer tourism months.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Kenora?
A: Kenora Airport is located approximately 6 kilometres (about 4 miles) east of the city centre, a 10-15 minute drive along Highway 17 East.

Q: Does the airport offer car rentals or parking on site?
A: Limited car rental services are available, and it is recommended to book in advance during peak season. Free or low-cost parking is available on site for travellers leaving vehicles during their trip.

Q: When is the busiest travel season at Kenora Airport?
A: Late spring through early fall is the busiest period, coinciding with fishing season and lake tourism. Winter traffic includes snowbirds and ice fishing enthusiasts traveling to remote lodges.
transport_tips: Taxis and pre-arranged shuttle services are the most reliable ground transport options, as public transit does not directly serve the airport. Renting a car is advisable for visitors planning to explore the surrounding lakes and remote fishing lodges, many of which are accessible only by vehicle or boat. If staying at a resort or camp, many operators offer complimentary pickup with advance notice.
local_tip: If you're flying in for a fishing trip, ship your tackle box and rods ahead via courier (e.g., Canada Post or UPS) to your lodge before you fly—most regional carriers have strict weight and sporting equipment restrictions, and checked baggage space on small turboprop flights can be very limited.
